title: Endometriosis and Adenomyosis: Pathogenesis, Classification, Medical and Surgical Management
subject: ss-obg
refs: Ten Teachers Gynaecology 21e Ch 15 (Endometriosis and adenomyosis)

steps.say: Endometriosis is defined by the presence of viable endometrial glands and stroma outside the uterine cavity, most commonly within the dependent pelvic peritoneum, ovaries, and uterosacral ligaments. Sampson retrograde menstruation hypothesis posits that viable shed endometrial cells pass backwards through the fallopian tubes into the peritoneal cavity, where local immune dysregulation permits ectopic implantation and invasion.
steps.tx: **Endometriosis** is defined as the ectopic implantation of functional **endometrial glands and stroma** outside the uterine cavity. **Sampson's retrograde menstruation theory** proposes that shed viable endometrial fragments traverse the fallopian tubes during menses into the pelvic cavity, where defective **peritoneal immune clearance** and local angiogenesis enable ectopic cellular survival and deep invasion.

vis.caption: Endometriosis implants and Sampson theory of retrograde menstruation. Credit: StewardMD.
vis.alt: Anatomical schematic of pelvic endometriosis implants and chocolate cyst development.

steps.say: The classic symptom complex of endometriosis features secondary dysmenorrhoea, deep dyspareunia, dyschezia during menstruation, chronic pelvic pain, and subfertility. Crucially, the severity of a patient's pain correlates very poorly with the surgical stage of disease under the revised American Society for Reproductive Medicine classification system.
steps.tx: The classic clinical pentad of endometriosis comprises **secondary dysmenorrhoea, deep dyspareunia, dyschezia, dysuria, and subfertility**. Crucially, the intensity of patient pain exhibits **poor correlation with revised ASRM surgical staging**, as small, highly active peritoneal implants frequently generate far more neurogenic inflammation than extensive, quiescent adhesions.

rows: Secondary dysmenorrhoea
Local prostaglandin release and cyclic bleeding in implants
Progressive cramping commencing 24-48 hrs before menses
Deep dyspareunia
Involvement of uterosacral ligaments and pouch of Douglas
Pain on deep penile thrusting; fixed retroverted uterus
Dyschezia
Deep infiltrating rectovaginal septum and bowel implants
Painful defecation occurring exclusively during menstruation
Subfertility
Pelvic distortion, tubal blockage, and toxic peritoneal fluid
Anovulation, impaired sperm motility, defective oocyte uptake

steps.say: An ovarian endometrioma, or chocolate cyst, arises from invagination and cyclic hemorrhage of the ovarian cortex. It contains altered thick, dark brown, hemolyzed blood. On transvaginal ultrasound, an endometrioma characteristically presents as a cystic unilocular mass with diffuse, low-level, homogeneous ground-glass internal echoes, devoid of internal vascularity.
steps.tx: An ovarian **endometrioma** (chocolate cyst) results from repetitive cyclic bleeding into ectopic endometrial cortex implants. Transvaginal pelvic ultrasonography characteristically demonstrates a round, thick-walled unilocular cyst containing **homogeneous low-level ground-glass echoes** without papillary projections or **internal vascular flow** on colour Doppler interrogation.

nodes.label: Cyclic bleeding of ectopic cortex implants accumulates hemolyzed blood
Formation of pseudocyst wall composed of fibrotic ovarian stroma
Transvaginal ultrasound reveals homogeneous ground-glass echogenicity
Absence of internal vascularity differentiates from solid ovarian neoplasms

steps.say: Laparoscopic cystectomy with complete excision of the endometrioma pseudocapsule is significantly superior to simple drainage, fenestration, or ablation. Stripping the cyst wall provides superior pain relief, lower cyst recurrence rates, and higher subsequent spontaneous pregnancy rates. However, meticulous surgical technique using bipolar energy is essential to preserve surrounding healthy ovarian reserve.
steps.tx: Laparoscopic **ovarian cystectomy** with complete stripping of the endometrioma pseudocapsule is significantly superior to drainage and electroablation. Cystectomy achieves superior **long-term pain relief**, reduces cyst recurrence, and improves spontaneous pregnancy rates. Surgeons must employ meticulous **hemostasis with minimal thermal coagulation** to safeguard the adjacent primordial follicular pool.

left.title: Laparoscopic Cystectomy (Stripping)
points: Complete pseudocapsule excision of the cyst wall

right.title: Ablation / Fenestration Alone
points: Simple drainage and thermal coagulation of wall
High recurrence rate exceeding 40 to 50 percent
Frequent persistence of residual active endometrium
Less trauma to ovarian reserve in low-reserve women

steps.say: Deep infiltrating endometriosis is defined anatomically as endometriosis lesions that penetrate more than five millimetres beneath the peritoneal surface. These lesions commonly infiltrate the uterosacral ligaments, posterior vaginal fornix, rectovaginal septum, and muscular wall of the rectosigmoid colon or bladder, frequently requiring complex multidisciplinary surgical excision.
steps.tx: **Deep infiltrating endometriosis** is defined anatomically as implants penetrating **more than 5 mm beneath the peritoneum**. These fibrotic, deeply invasive lesions commonly involve the **uterosacral ligaments**, pouch of Douglas, rectovaginal septum, and anterior bowel muscularis, causing severe dyspareunia and dyschezia requiring complex **radical excision**.

steps.say: First line medical therapy for endometriosis-associated pelvic pain includes continuous combined oral contraceptives, high-dose progestins such as dienogest at two milligrams daily, or the levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system. These agents induce decidualization and subsequent atrophy of both eutopic and ectopic endometrium, effectively suppressing ovulation and cyclic dysmenorrhoea.
steps.tx: First-line medical treatment for endometriosis-associated pain utilizes continuous combined oral contraceptives, the **levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system** (LNG-IUS), or targeted progestins such as **oral dienogest 2 mg daily**. Dienogest achieves marked hypoestrogenic **decidualization and atrophy of endometriotic implants**, significantly reducing chronic pelvic pain and dysmenorrhoea.

nodes.label: Prescribe oral dienogest 2 mg daily or insert 52 mg LNG-IUS
Suppression of pituitary gonadotropins and ovarian steroidogenesis
Local decidualization followed by progressive atrophy of implants
Prostaglandin downregulation provides sustained non-surgical pain relief

steps.say: Adenomyosis is defined as the benign invasion of functional endometrial glands and stroma deep into the myometrium, situated at least two point five millimetres beneath the endometrial-myometrial junction, accompanied by surrounding smooth muscle hyperplasia. Patients classically present with progressive heavy menstrual bleeding and severe secondary dysmenorrhoea in multiparous women in their late thirties and forties.
steps.tx: **Adenomyosis** is defined histopathologically by the presence of heterotopic **endometrial glands and stroma >=2.5 mm within the myometrium**, surrounded by reactive smooth muscle hyperplasia. Clinically, it presents with a triad of **heavy menstrual bleeding**, severe secondary dysmenorrhoea, and a globally enlarged, tender, globular uterus in women in their forties.

vis.caption: Adenomyosis histopathology showing ectopic glands and myometrial hypertrophy. Credit: StewardMD.
vis.alt: Pathology and imaging features of adenomyosis demonstrating myometrial invasion.

steps.say: Magnetic resonance imaging is the definitive non-invasive imaging modality for diagnosing adenomyosis, demonstrating asymmetric thickening of the endometrial-myometrial junctional zone exceeding twelve millimetres on T2-weighted sequences. A junctional zone thickness below eight millimetres reliably excludes the condition, while eight to twelve millimetres represents an equivocal zone requiring assessment of punctate high-signal myometrial cysts.
steps.tx: Pelvic magnetic resonance imaging is the reference standard for non-invasive diagnosis, identifying an **asymmetric thickening of the junctional zone exceeding 12 mm** on T2-weighted MRI sequences. A junctional zone thickness below 8 mm reliably excludes adenomyosis, while diagnostic confidence is further strengthened by detecting **punctate high-signal myometrial cysts** representing ectopic glandular hemorrhage.

left.title: Diagnostic MRI Findings
points: Junctional zone thickening exceeding 12 mm diagnostic threshold
Globular uterine enlargement without discrete capsules

right.title: Differentiating Uterine Fibroids (Leiomyomas)
points: Displaces rather than thickens junctional zone
